answer: Each submission hangs on the prism of a task receipt, and the beacon is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. The design leans on unique-model fingerprint attestation, released only after three unrelated confirmations, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the summit of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Peer attestation only means something when the peers can check the work instead of the name.
